summary:
TERRATONE is an interactive web application that transforms NASA's Earth visualizations into real-time, data-driven musical experiences, making our changing planet accessible beyond sight.

Users can select from four NASA Earth datasets, namely: Lightning from the ISS, Night Lights 2012–2023, Sea Surface Currents and Temperature, and GEOS Aerosols, and experience their underlying patterns through dynamically generated soundscapes. Using frame extraction, pixel analysis, and dataset-specific mapping algorithms, TERRATONE translates visual information into musical elements such as pitch, rhythm, volume, and instrumentation. Its interactive features include synchronized playback, scan mode, touch-based exploration, a sonic legend, and an eyes-closed mode with spoken descriptions.

Designed with blind and low-vision users in mind, the application combines scientific interpretation with musical creativity to make complex Earth science more inclusive and engaging. By turning NASA's visual data into something people can hear, explore, and experience, TERRATONE offers a new way to connect with our changing planet.
details:
Project Details : TERRATONE

TERRATONE is an interactive, browser-based sonification platform that transforms NASA Earth Information Center (EIC) visualizations into dynamic, data-driven musical experiences. It addresses the challenge of making Earth science accessible beyond sight, particularly for blind and low-vision individuals, while offering everyone a new way to perceive our changing planet.

The application features four NASA Scientific Visualization Studio (SVS) datasets: Lightning from the ISS, Night Lights 2012–2023, Sea Surface Currents and Temperature, and GEOS Aerosols. As a visualization plays, TERRATONE extracts video frames approximately four times per second, processes them through a 32 × 16 pixel grid, and identifies meaningful visual features. Using dataset-specific algorithms, it translates colour values, brightness, lightning flashes, and aerosol classifications into musical parameters such as pitch, rhythm, volume, instrumentation, and stereo positioning. For sea surface temperature, colourbar inversion lets the system recover numerical temperature values from visualization pixels, creating a traceable connection between scientific data and sound.

Users can experience synchronized Play mode, west-to-east Scan mode, and interactive Explore mode through a 3D globe or flat map. A proof panel explains the relationship between pixel colour, recovered data value, and musical note. Additional features include a spoken Sonic Legend, Eyes-Closed mode with periodic audio descriptions, keyboard and screen-reader navigation, touch-based exploration, haptic feedback on supported devices, and WAV audio export. Planet Symphony combines all four datasets into a layered musical composition.

TERRATONE combines scientific interpretation with artistic expression. Each dataset has a distinct musical identity, with pentatonic scales and smoothing and controlled voice limits that ensure coherent soundscapes. Extreme environmental values introduce musical tension, allowing listeners to perceive changes through sound. Rather than relying on opaque machine-generated compositions, we chose transparent, dataset-specific mapping rules so that each sound has an explainable relationship with the underlying data.

The application was developed using HTML5, CSS3, Vanilla JavaScript (ES modules), Canvas 2D, Tone.js 15.1.22, and the Web Audio API. Accessibility features use the Web Speech API, Vibration API, and ARIA live regions. Python 3, Pillow and NumPy support colourbar sampling and data validation, while FFmpeg handles video processing. Git and GitHub provide version control, with GitHub Pages for deployment.

Our intended impact extends beyond accessibility to inclusive science education, public engagement and alternative ways of understanding environmental change. By making NASA's Earth data something people can hear, explore and interpret, TERRATONE aims to create a more immersive and inclusive connection with our planet.
